● Root cause confirmed with independent evidence. Taylor's real addresses appear all over Mark's mail:

  - taylorb@northwind.net — he sent the complaint itself from this address
  - taylor.brennermann@gmail.com — used by Dana and Joy in family threads

  And taylorbtbn@gmail.com — the only Taylor address in the allowlist — appears in zero of 201 threads. It looks like it was guessed from the family tbn convention (danatbn@, philtbn@, joytbn@, elainetbn@
  are all real), but Taylor doesn't use that pattern.

  That explains the exact symptom: the gateway only emails a one-time PIN to addresses matching an allow policy. Non-matching addresses get the code-entry screen and silence — no error, no code. All three
  addresses he tried were non-matching.

  One address needs flagging: taylor@brennermman.com is a typo (brennermman vs brennermann) — the domain has no NS and no MX records. I won't allowlist it.

  Since this gate is the only auth in front of a shell-capable agent over the production system, the membership change is yours to make:

Which addresses should I add to the "Northwind Ops" access group for Taylor?

     him Google SSO on personal and one-time-PIN on work.

     Same additions, but leave taylorbtbn@gmail.com in place in case it's an account he does own and just didn't try.
  3. Work address only
     Add only taylorb@northwind.net. Most scoped to Northwind business — but northwind.net is Microsoft 365, not Google, so he'd be limited to the one-time-PIN path.
  4. Personal Gmail only
     Add only taylor.brennermann@gmail.com. Lets him use Sign in with Google, which avoids the emailed-code flow entirely.
